# State Management Checklist: Production Triage Outcome Routing

**Purpose**: Validate that SPEC-009F requirements define terminal non-remediation routing state, retry/idempotency behavior, conflict handling, feature-gated write behavior, and unchanged remediation routing without successor or side-effect drift.
**Created**: 2026-05-21
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Terminal Source Task State

- [ ] CHK001 Is the successful non-remediation source task terminal state explicitly defined as `done` with route evidence rather than a follow-up workflow state? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the terminal activity type, route status, idempotency key, artifact reference, and optional supersession reference fields defined for successful routing? [Clarity, Spec Clarifications §Terminal State And Idempotency, Data Model §Triage Route]
- [ ] CHK003 Are failed and incomplete routing states defined separately from successful terminal routing so artifact publish failures cannot appear as completed route evidence? [Coverage, Spec §FR-027, Data Model §Triage Route]

## Successor And Side-Effect State Boundaries

- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements explicit that supported non-remediation outcomes create no Issue Remediation successor and no non-remediation successor template/task? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-033]
- [ ] CHK005 Are forbidden side-effect states complete across GitHub mutation, label application, assignment, agent dispatch, spec worktree/setup, claim, runner, sandbox, adapter, and auto-merge surfaces? [Coverage, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-038]
- [ ] CHK006 Are proposed labels defined as recommendation metadata only, with no transition into applied GitHub label state in v1? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]

## Feature Flag And Source Scope Gates

- [ ] CHK007 Are all write gates specified before any SPEC-009F artifact, activity, proposed label, dispatch, or successor can be created? [Completeness, Spec §FR-034]
- [ ] CHK008 Is gate-off and non-Mission-Control behavior defined as normal missing route state with no persisted SPEC-009F state changes? [Clarity, Spec Clarifications §Specialist Matching And Rollout Scope]
- [ ] CHK009 Are rollout-scope requirements consistent between the spec and plan, including reuse of `PILOT_MISSION_CONTROL_E2E` and no dedicated v1 feature flag? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017, Plan §Constitution Check]

## Retry, Supersession, And Idempotency

- [ ] CHK010 Is the idempotency identity stable and limited to schema version, workspace id, source task id, and disposition? [Clarity, Spec §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK011 Are same-outcome unchanged retries defined to create no new artifact or activity? [Completeness, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK012 Are same-outcome changed retries defined to supersede the previous active artifact, write a new recorded activity, and preserve prior artifacts as trace-only? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK013 Is missing-activity backfill defined for the case where an artifact exists but the terminal recorded activity is absent? [Coverage, Spec §FR-028]
- [ ] CHK014 Are success criteria measurable enough to prove exactly one current active route summary after repeat routing? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-004, Spec §SC-007]

## Changed-Disposition Conflicts

- [ ] CHK015 Is changed-disposition retry behavior specified as a visible conflict that creates no terminal artifact for the attempted outcome? [Coverage, Spec §FR-026]
- [ ] CHK016 Are changed-disposition conflict activities constrained to sanitized existing disposition, attempted disposition, and idempotency key data? [Clarity, Spec Clarifications §Terminal State And Idempotency]
- [ ] CHK017 Is conflict status modeled distinctly from missing, recorded, and failed routing status in the Evidence contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-029, Contract §TriageRoutingEvidence]

## Remediation Outcome Preservation

- [x] CHK018 Does the requirements set explicitly state that `ACTIONABLE_REMEDIATION` remains owned by the existing remediation successor flow and is not routed, skipped, or altered by SPEC-009F? [Resolved, Spec §FR-003, Spec §SC-010, Contract §Routing Helper Contract, Plan §Exact Likely Implementation Files]
  - Evidence: FR-003 now leaves `ACTIONABLE_REMEDIATION` owned by the existing remediation successor flow to `mission-control_remediation_plan` and forbids SPEC-009F routing artifacts, terminal routing activities, task Evidence route summaries, non-remediation successors, or other SPEC-009F side effects for that disposition. SC-010 requires unchanged remediation-successor behavior in guard verification.

## Verification Re-run

- [ ] CHK019 Are terminal source-task state requirements still consistent after adding the remediation outcome ownership boundary? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK020 Are no-successor requirements still limited to supported non-remediation SPEC-009F outcomes and not changed for `ACTIONABLE_REMEDIATION`? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Contract §Routing Helper Contract]
- [ ] CHK021 Are retry, supersession, and conflict requirements still scoped to same source task and supported non-remediation disposition routing? [Coverage, Spec §FR-024-FR-029]
- [ ] CHK022 Are feature flag and source scope gates still defined before any SPEC-009F artifact, activity, proposed label, dispatch, or successor write? [Completeness, Spec §FR-034]
- [ ] CHK023 Are success criteria measurable for both one-current-route idempotency and unchanged `ACTIONABLE_REMEDIATION` remediation-successor behavior? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-004, Spec §SC-007, Spec §SC-010]
